question: Find the inverse of $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\3&2\end{bmatrix}$.
explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the determinant
For the given matrix, $$|A|=(2)(2)-(1)(3)=1$$
Step 2: Check invertibility
Since $|A|=1\ne0$, the inverse of $A$ exists.
Step 3: Find the adjoint
Interchanging the diagonal elements and changing the signs of the other elements gives $$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\-3&2\end{bmatrix}$$
Step 4: Use the inverse relation
Since $A^{-1}=\frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A$, $$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\-3&2\end{bmatrix}$$
